pages.text: Two electric blocks connect when they touch through faces that both accept power. A generator accepts power on every face, but many machines only on one: the motor, the lamps and the polarizer use their $(item)back$() face. Each chapter says which face to use.

$(l)Cable hubs$()$(br)A cable hub is a full block that connects on $(item)all six faces$(). Stack them to run power through walls and floors. Each hub handles up to $(item)5,000 V$() and has a $(item)current limit$(), checked against the total current of the $(item)whole network$():

$(li)Copper Cable Hub: $(item)16 A$()$(li)Brass Cable Hub: $(item)50 A$()$(li)Aluminum Cable Hub: $(item)80 A$()$(li)Steel Casing Cable Hub and Heavy Cable Hub: $(item)100 A$()$(li)Steel Cable Hub: $(item)250 A$()$(br2)Copper hubs are the cheapest, two per craft from copper ingots and copper wire. Upgrade them before your network grows past their limit, or they will burn out (see $(item)Overloads$()).
